A1.justification: Both PDFs describe QAEncoder and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–J. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of equations, figures and tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval experiments on BEIR, FIGNEWS and CRUD-RAG, together with method ablations, query-generator robustness tests and embedding analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and the appendices, including retrieval comparisons and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same query-embedding averaging and embedding, textual and hybrid fingerprint procedures. Appendix G adds BEIR prompting information without establishing a revision to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same fifteen BEIR datasets, FIGNEWS in five languages and Chinese CRUD-RAG. The added discussion of declarative BEIR queries does not introduce new evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main and appendix tables, including BM25, DocT5Query, dense encoder backbones, GPL, fine-tuned models, HyDE, Query2Doc and QA-RAG.

E3.justification: Previously stated query sampling, metrics, hyperparameter searches and training budgets remain unchanged. Appendix G newly documents BEIR few-shot prompting; it does not report switching from a previously specified BEIR protocol. Appendix B's zero-shot statement concerns the latest news datasets in both versions.

E4.justification: The fingerprint ablations, hyperparameter and query-count analyses, generator robustness experiments, embedding case studies and normality analyses are retained unchanged. The Appendix G addition supplies explanation without new analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including Appendix A.3.3's Q-Q assessment and Anderson-Darling tests. Neither version adds or revises repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or uncertainty-reporting practices relative to the other.

E6.justification: All tabulated results and plotted findings remain unchanged, including Appendix J. Figure 5 retains the same similarity values; its numerical labels change size only.

T1.justification: The conical distribution hypothesis, method equations, Gaussian assumptions, Theorem 1 and appendix proofs and definitions are unchanged. The new fingerprint analogy introduces no formal mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free alignment, document fingerprints, theoretical grounding, generalization and compatibility with RAG systems.

C2.justification: Appendix G newly explains that generated declarative BEIR queries resemble natural inputs and can play a role analogous to document fingerprints. This adds a limited mechanism interpretation; the existing results discussion and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix G newly discloses few-shot in-context prompting for generating declarative BEIR queries. v2 lacked this benchmark-specific detail. Exact few-shot demonstrations are still absent, and other implementation and resource-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and related-work discussion are unchanged. The added Appendix G passage neither cites additional research nor revises the paper's positioning relative to earlier methods.

P1.justification: Author affiliations and contact information are updated, 'English version' becomes 'English prompts,' and Appendix G gains a short explanatory passage. The remaining prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 5 uses smaller, slightly repositioned heatmap cell-value labels. The author block and spacing around Appendix G also change locally; figures, tables and the overall layout otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Appendix G improves transparency by documenting BEIR-specific few-shot generation of declarative queries and explaining its intended connection to document fingerprints. The benefit is limited because the actual demonstrations remain unspecified, while the methods, empirical evidence and theory are unchanged. The small presentation edits introduce no material overall harm.
